The test image shows a tomato stem with scattered white/pale crusty spots along it. The stem is hairy (typical of tomato), with discrete white lesion-like spots distributed along the stem. Leaves appear slightly distorted. The key diagnostic feature is those white/pale spots on the stem.

Top candidates: Powdery_Mildew (white powdery patches on stem), Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato (stem lesions), or Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato.

Using my 1 reference view on Powdery_Mildew to check the white stem spots pattern.

The Powdery_Mildew reference shows white discrete spots/patches on tomato leaf surfaces — this is consistent with what I see in the test image. The test image shows white surface-level spots on the tomato stem (not deep lesions or dark discoloration), and powdery mildew is known to infect stems as well as leaves, appearing as white powdery patches. The discrete white spots in the test image align well with powdery mildew on a hairy tomato stem.

The main alternatives (bacterial canker would show more sunken brown stem cankers; bacterial speck would show dark spots on leaves) are less consistent with the white surface spots seen here.
